accuracyFacts: The stable compiler is TypeScript 7.0 as of 2026-11-16; TypeScript 7.1 is beta. Clearly label beta behavior and do not present it as stable.

A file with a top-level import or export is a module; moduleDetection may also classify files as modules based on package.json type and other project context. A file with no module indicator may contribute declarations to a shared script/global scope.

Type-only import/export syntax is erased from JavaScript output. With verbatimModuleSyntax, import/export modifiers communicate whether syntax is preserved or erased; imports lacking type modifiers are not silently elided as type-only uses.
A declaration file describes a runtime API but supplies no implementation. Ambient declarations and module declarations are not evidence that a runtime module or global actually exists.

Module augmentation resolves its module specifier like an import/export, must augment an existing named export, cannot add new top-level declarations, and cannot augment a default export. Runtime implementation still must be installed/executed.

Declaration merging has ordered rules and conflicts: interfaces merge compatible members, namespaces can merge with classes/functions/enums in supported orders, and class/interface declarations do not generally merge as an arbitrary pair.

NodeNext follows current Node.js module behavior and can change across TypeScript versions; node16/node18/node20 modes model fixed Node versions. Bundler mode supports package exports/imports and extensionless relative paths but does not enforce all Node ESM path constraints.

The module option and moduleResolution work together to determine emitted form and package conditions. Node16/node18/node20/NodeNext must pair with corresponding resolution modes; bundler pairs with esnext or preserve; preserve implies bundler resolution.

In Node-aware and bundler resolution, package exports/imports may control reachable paths and condition selection. The types condition and runtime condition ordering must be designed so TypeScript and runtime resolve compatible implementations; typesVersions is generally a fallback when exports are absent for package resolution.

The package types/typings fields point to declaration entry points; exports can encapsulate subpaths and use conditional types/runtime targets. typesVersions redirects declarations by compiler version only in supported resolution contexts and does not override exports.
baseUrl is deprecated in TypeScript 6.0 and is no longer a lookup root in TypeScript 7.0; paths does not rewrite emitted specifiers and must match the runtime/bundler mapping separately.

preserveValueImports and importsNotUsedAsValues were deprecated in TypeScript 5.5 in favor of verbatimModuleSyntax; TypeScript 6.0 and 7.0 remove/deprecate legacy module options including classic and node10 module resolution.
Declaration emit generates .d.ts descriptions from source; declarationMap adds map files for editor navigation and does not change runtime code.
